summary: Mount Pacifico's 1932 open lookout tower with no cab, known from one 1932 Los Angeles Times story and a photo; removal unknown and summit metal posts unconfirmed.

facts.design: Open tower with steel rungs to a small platform (1932 Los Angeles Times story, as quoted by Angeles Adventures); no cab, per Angeles Adventures' comparison with other San Gabriel lookouts
facts.status_note: Register lists removal as Unknown; a visitor found possible metal posts on the summit but could not link them to the lookout
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Angeles National Forest

access.note: Wikipedia describes the summit as reached by the Pacific Crest Trail on Angeles National Forest land; no source says whether the lookout site itself is open

visit.trail_note: The Pacific Crest Trail is the main hiking route to the summit; Wikipedia describes a strenuous 11.9-mile route

events.note: Register gives 1932; the December 4, 1932 Los Angeles Times story is the only source for the structure (as quoted by Angeles Adventures)
Structure not listed in Mark V. Thornton's 1986 Fire Lookout Inventory
Registered November 3, 2019 as US 1786, CA 32; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.why: The register lists removal as Unknown and no source records the structure coming down; the only later detail is possible metal posts on the summit, which the writer could not link to the lookout

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives the site 7,114 ft (2,168 m); Wikipedia gives the peak 7,129 ft (2,173 m). The record keeps the register figure and the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Thin: the 1932 Los Angeles Times story is known only as quoted by Angeles Adventures and the register; I did not see the original article. The summit metal posts and drill holes are one visitor's observations and are not confirmed as lookout remains. The register's elevation (7,114 ft) and Wikipedia's (7,129 ft) differ. The brief's gone status is not supported (see corrections).
